newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up on selective buying.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed higher on Monday, boosted by demand for issues expected to post strong results for 1996 and speculative buying of domestic A shares, brokers said.
The foreign currency B share index rose 2.07 points or 1.44 percent to end at 145.23 on turnover of HK$60.61 million against the previous session's HK$53.63 million.
The index of A shares for domestic investors gained 4.54 points or 1.31 percent to close at 351.17 on turnover of 5.01 billion yuan compared with 4.28 billion last Friday.

Investors were seen cautiously building up positions in B shares of firms likely to report strong results, and sentiment was also helped by the relatively strong performance of the A share market, brokers said.

"The rise in the A share market was linked to strong gains in shares of utilities firms, which are mostly index-weighted counters," a broker at China Securities Co Ltd said. "But trading remained speculative."
On the B share market, conglomerate Lionda put in the strongest performance with a rise of HK$0.30 or 8.22 percent to HK$3.95 on volume of 468,400 shares on speculative buying.
Building materials producer Shenzhen Fangda firmed HK$0.40 or 4.85 percent to HK$8.64 on trade of 836,499 shares due to investor optimism over the company's prospects, brokers said.
Hotelier Dadonghai, the most active issue, edged up HK$0.05 to HK$3.70 after 1.06 million shares were traded.
Guangdong Power inched up HK$0.01 to HK$6.90 on volume of 1.05 million shares. There was market talk that the electricity supplier would report a sharp rise in its profits for 1996, brokers said.
Refrigerator maker Hefei Meilin gained HK$0.12 to HK$5.65, with 512,900 shares changing hands.
On the A share market, power supplier Zhuhai Huadian closed at its 10 percent limit-up at 4.90 yuan due to speculative buying, brokers said.
Lionda followed suit, soared 0.78 yuan to 8.60 yuan as 5.80 million shares changed hands.
